title: Partial updates with field masks
summary: Keep the value and the update intent in separate fields of a PATCH request.
content:
u/SnooSongs6758 asked on r/golang:

I’m creating a REST API using Golang v1.25, Gin v1.10.0, and Validator v10.20.0. I have a PATCH endpoint where, when the address attribute is:

  • undefined -> keep the original data
  • null -> delete the original data
  • contains something -> replace the original data with the new

Right now I’m using a pointer for it, so I can know when it’s null. The problem is that I couldn’t find a way to differentiate when the attribute is undefined or null.

Does anyone know a way to check if a specific attribute is undefined?

While the answers there explore how to support this case, I think we can simplify the design and make our lives considerably easier. Currently the address field does this:

  • a string value updates the stored address in place
  • null deletes the stored address
  • and undefined signals a missing value, which keeps the original data

It’s mixing value and intent within a single field. We can use address for the plain value and another field, update_mask, to list the fields the client wants to change. Google’s API design guide calls this a field mask. Protobuf has the same thing as its FieldMask type.

Over HTTP, the client sends a PATCH with the new values in the body and the mask in the update_mask query parameter, like ?update_mask=name,address. The server changes only the fields named in the mask.

Say the server has this user stored. Each request below starts from it:

{"id":"1","name":"Alice","address":"Old Street 1"}

To update the address, the client sets the update_mask query parameter to address and sends the new value in the body. The server changes the address and returns the updated user:

# request
PATCH /users/1?update_mask=address HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{"address": "New Street 2"}

# response
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"1","name":"Alice","address":"New Street 2"}

To delete the address, the query parameter stays update_mask=address, and the body sends null:

# request
PATCH /users/1?update_mask=address HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{"address": null}

# response
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"1","name":"Alice","address":""}

An empty body, {}, does the same thing, because address is still in the mask.

If the client only wants to change the name, it sends update_mask=name. The server leaves address alone because the mask doesn’t name it:

# request
PATCH /users/1?update_mask=name HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": "Bob"}

# response
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"1","name":"Bob","address":"Old Street 1"}

On the Go side, the asker used a pointer so the handler could see null. With pointers, the struct looks like this:

type User struct {
    ID      string  `json:"id"`
    Name    *string `json:"name"`
    Address *string `json:"address"`
}

A nil Address can mean the client sent null, or it can mean the client didn’t send the key at all. That’s the problem from the question.

With the mask, the handler doesn’t need to tell them apart:

  • address in the mask and a string in the body: the address gets updated
  • address in the mask and null or no key in the body: the decoded address is "", so the address gets cleared
  • address not in the mask: the handler ignores the address in the body

None of these cases need nil, so plain strings are enough:

type User struct {
    ID      string `json:"id"`
    Name    string `json:"name"`
    Address string `json:"address"`
}

In the handler, in is the request body and u is the stored user. The loop goes through the mask and copies each named field from in to u. An unknown field name gets a 400:

func (s *Server) patchUser(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    mask := r.URL.Query().Get("update_mask")
    // ...

    var in User

    // json v2 API
    if err := json.UnmarshalRead(r.Body, &in); err != nil {
        http.Error(w, "invalid JSON body", http.StatusBadRequest)
        return
    }

    // ...
    u, ok := s.users[r.PathValue("id")]
    // ...

    for path := range strings.SplitSeq(mask, ",") {
        switch path {
        case "name":
            u.Name = in.Name
        case "address":
            u.Address = in.Address
        default:
            http.Error(w, "unknown field in update_mask: "+path,
                http.StatusBadRequest)
            return
        }
    }
    s.users[u.ID] = u
    // ...
}

Important

The handler only mutates the fields named in the mask. Every other field on the stored user stays as it was, even if the body sends a value for it.

So far address has been a string. If it were an object with street and city, a client might want to change only the city. A mask with address covers the whole object. To target only the city, the query parameter names the subfield with a dot, as update_mask=address.city:

# request
PATCH /users/1?update_mask=address.city HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{"address": {"city": "Berlin"}}

The handler then needs an address.city case in its switch.

The full example with a test is on GitHub.
